solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Excessively sentimental message shortened

indicators.note: shortened says the message word loses its final letter

parts.note: a tweet is a short message posted on social media

explanation.surface: A gushing note that has been trimmed down for being too soppy.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee is a British word for something cloyingly sweet, quaint or sentimental to excess.

clue.text: Part of church school — one removed faulty step

indicators.note: removed says the numeral for one is taken out of the word for school

parts.note: to school someone is to train them
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: faulty says the letters of step are wrongly ordered and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A church school reports a pupil who was hurt by a broken step.
explanation.definitionFit: The transept is the cross-arm of a cruciform church, crossing the nave.

clue.text: Run more

definitions.meaning: in cricket, a run not credited to the batsman, such as a wide or bye
more as in additional, over and above

explanation.surface: An order to keep running further.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a bye or wide is scored as an extra; as an adjective the word means additional.

clue.text: Information given before summit in bureaucratic language

indicators.note: given before says the information word comes ahead of the summit word

parts.note: news is information about recent events
a summit is a peak

explanation.surface: Briefings handed out ahead of a summit meeting, full of official jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's term from Nineteen Eighty-Four now describes evasive, ambiguous official jargon.

clue.text: Release former partner, almost lacking emotion

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: almost says the word for lacking emotion loses its last letter

parts.note: empty can mean devoid of feeling

explanation.surface: Someone lets an old flame go, feeling almost nothing about it.
explanation.definitionFit: To exempt someone is to free them from a duty or obligation.

clue.text: Discount kindness as a redeeming feature

parts.note: a discount on a price is a saving
grace can mean kindness or goodwill shown to others

explanation.surface: A shop's money-off offer and friendly manner make up for its other failings.
explanation.definitionFit: A saving grace is the one good quality that compensates for someone's faults.

clue.text: Individual, first off, has me engaged, a US poet

indicators.note: engaged means held inside, so me sits within what remains
first off says the opening letter of the word for individual is dropped

parts.note: an individual is a person

explanation.surface: An American poet tells how someone became engaged to him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first off' turns PERSON into ERSON, and ME is 'engaged' in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was a nineteenth-century American essayist and poet of the Transcendentalist movement.

clue.text: Peck: his last is first in sequence

indicators.note: his refers back to Peck, so his last means the final letter of that word
first in picks the opening letter of the word sequence

explanation.surface: A puzzle about Gregory Peck: his final film comes first in the running order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peck' does double duty: it is the definition, and 'his last' takes its final letter K. Then IS as written and S from 'first in sequence'.
explanation.definitionFit: A peck is a quick light kiss, as a bird's beak touches briefly.

clue.text: Perhaps a recital to be broadcast

definitions.note: a is one example of the indefinite kind of this part of speech, hence perhaps

indicators.note: to be broadcast suggests scattering, so the letters of recital are spread out and rearranged

explanation.surface: A recital that may be put out on radio.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'a' is the indefinite article, an example of the class signalled by perhaps.

clue.text: Zimbalist originally wearing necktie in a moving picture

indicators.note: wearing says the letter is dressed in, so sits inside, the other letters
moving says the letters of necktie in a are shifted around
originally picks the opening letter of the name Zimbalist

explanation.surface: The actor Zimbalist sports a tie on screen in a film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving picture' reads as one phrase, a film, but 'moving' is the anagram signal and only 'picture' defines; 'wearing' puts Z inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Orson Welles's 1941 film is a picture in the sense of a motion picture.

clue.text: Struggles to accept western opinions

indicators.note: to accept says the struggles word takes the western letter inside it

parts.note: vies means competes or struggles

explanation.surface: Someone battles to come round to Western ways of thinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Views are opinions or points of view held about something.

clue.text: Sergeant Major cultivated? Rubbish, a know-it-all

parts.note: arty means affecting artistic or cultured tastes
pants is British slang for rubbish, as in 'that film was pants'

explanation.surface: A sergeant major asks whether he is cultured, then dismisses the idea as nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Smarty-pants is an informal, mocking name for someone who shows off how much they know.

clue.text: Principal character in a line

parts.note: a card is an eccentric or amusing character

explanation.surface: The lead role in a play written in a single line.
explanation.definitionFit: Cardinal as an adjective means of chief importance, as in cardinal sins or points.

clue.text: Square Italian dish containing anchovies, primarily

indicators.note: containing says the dish word holds that letter inside it

parts.note: a pizza is an Italian dish

indicators.note: primarily picks the opening letter of anchovies

explanation.surface: A pizza topped with anchovies, cut into squares.
explanation.definitionFit: A piazza is a public square or open space in an Italian town.

clue.text: Movement round university where lots go

indicators.note: round says the movement word goes around the university letter

parts.note: action is movement or activity

explanation.surface: Lots of people head off around the university campus.
explanation.definitionFit: Lots are the items offered for bidding at a sale, which go under the hammer there.

clue.text: Timetable information ringed by a District Attorney

indicators.note: ringed by says the information word is surrounded by the other letters

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A District Attorney has the schedule details circled.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list or schedule of items to be dealt with, a plan of business.

clue.text: Diligent American leaving for workshop

indicators.note: leaving says the American letters depart from the diligent word

parts.note: studious means diligent in study

explanation.surface: A hard-working American quits to go to a workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is an artist's or craftsman's workroom.

clue.text: Forced, prisoners exercised

parts.note: cons is slang for convicts or prisoners
trained can mean exercised, as in working out

explanation.surface: Prison inmates were made to do exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Constrained means compelled or restricted, made to act against one's will.

clue.text: Wayfarer with small number on loco

indicators.note: on in a down clue says the first piece is placed above the second

parts.note: NO is the short form of number
loco is slang for crazy or mad

explanation.surface: A traveller rides a train with a low-numbered locomotive.
explanation.definitionFit: A nomad is a wanderer with no fixed home, a traveller by way of life.

clue.text: Touch lucky, at first, after charge

indicators.note: after says the lucky letter follows the charge word

parts.note: a fee is a charge for a service

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of lucky

explanation.surface: A lucky touch comes after a fee has been paid.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel something is to touch it, sensing it with the hands.

clue.text: Girl in care, I suspect

indicators.note: suspect means doubtful or dodgy, so these letters are not in their proper order

explanation.surface: A child in care, so I suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a girl's name, the kind of first name crosswords call a girl.

clue.text: A modern resort? You wish!

indicators.note: resort, read as re-sort, says the letters of a modern are sorted again

explanation.surface: A sarcastic reply to someone hoping for an up-to-date holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday destination, but it is read as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are dismissive retorts telling someone their hope will never come true.

clue.text: Legendary knight in a cell, not free

indicators.note: free means loose, so these letters can be set free and rearranged

explanation.surface: A knight of legend locked up in a cell, no longer at liberty.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the foremost knight of King Arthur's Round Table, lover of Guinevere.

clue.text: Reportedly lazy superstar

indicators.note: reportedly says the word for lazy is to be heard, not seen, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: idle means lazy

explanation.surface: A celebrity said to be a layabout.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a hugely admired celebrity, the object of fans' adoration.
